task.question: What temperature was recorded in Lingwood, Norfolk during the June heat record in the United Kingdom in 2026?
task.evidence: The June heat record is broken for a third consecutive day, with 38 °C recorded in Lingwood, Norfolk.

answer:
During the heatwave on 26 June 2026, a temperature of 38.0 °C (100.4 °F) was recorded at a Met Office station in Lingwood, Norfolk, breaking the all-time United Kingdom temperature record for the month of June.

FINAL: 38.0

[2026 European heatwaves]

Starting in late May, severe heatwaves affected Europe. Temperature records were broken in 18 countries. The first heatwave began on 24 May, with temperatures higher than normal and heat-related deaths. Temperatures were the highest ever recorded for May, starting Central Europe's summer earlier than usual. Western Europe was the most affected.

A second, more severe heatwave began on 17 June. On 26 June, the World Meteorological Organization said the heatwave was expected to affect Western Europe, Central Europe and Southern Europe over the following two weeks. By 5 July, over 5,600 excess deaths were reported.

A third heatwave began on 4 July in the United Kingdom. The UK Health Security Agency issued heat-health alerts. Official heatwave conditions started 6 July in parts of southeastern England that exceeded 28° for the third consecutive day. Temperatures peaked at 35.5° in Wisley, Surrey, on 9 July, the eighth day above 34 °C (93.2 °F), a UK record for the most days exceeding that temperature in a single year. The duration of this heatwave led to 'extreme' marine heatwaves, affecting the southern North Sea and parts of the English Channel.

The heat triggered forest fires and widespread drought. The Elbe, Rhine and Danube experienced a severe drought, including a record shallowness in the Balkans on 10 August. The increased water temperature raised concerns over rivers becoming too hot and shallow for nuclear power stations to use for cooling.

[Lingwood]

Lingwood is a village and former civil parish, now in the parish of Lingwood and Burlingham, in the Broadland district, in the English county of Norfolk. In 2011 the built-up area had a population of 2,719 and the built-up area sub division had a population of 2,493.

Lingwood is located 2.3 miles (3.7 km) south-west of Acle and 8 miles (13 km) east of Norwich.

History

Lingwood's name is of Anglo-Saxon origin and derives from the Old English for bank wood.

Lingwood is not listed in the Domesday Book.

In 1931 the parish had a population of 568. On 1 April 1935 the parish was abolished and merged with Burlingham.

Lingwood Railway Station opened in 1882 on the Great Eastern Railway and remains open as a stop on the Wherry Line for services between Norwich and Great Yarmouth.

During a heatwave on 26 June 2026, a temperature of 38.0 °C (100.4 °F) was recorded at a Met Office station in Lingwood, breaking the all-time United Kingdom temperature record for the month of June. This comprehensively beat the previous record of 35.6 °C (96.1 °F), set in the 1976 heatwave.

St. Peter's Church

Lingwood's former parish church is dedicated to Saint Peter and dates from the Fourteenth Century. St. Peter's is located on Church Road and has been Grade I listed since 1962. The church is open for Sunday service three times a month.

St. Peter's holds a set of royal arms from the reign of King George IV as well as a medieval wall painting of Saint Christopher which was uncovered in 1965.

Governance

Lingwood is part of the electoral ward of Burlingham for local elections and is part of the district of Broadland.
